title: Find another angle with same position
text: Notice that $$\frac{7\pi}{3}$$ is larger than one full rotation of $$2\pi$$. $$We$$ $$can$$ $$subtract$$ $$2\pi$$ (which is equivalent to $$\frac{6\pi}{3}\$\$)$$ $$to$$ $$find$$ $$a$$ $$simplier$$ $$angle$$ $$on$$ $$the$$ $$primary$$ $$unit$$ $$circle$$ $$that$$ $$is$$ $$at$$ $$the$$ $$same$$ $$position$$.

title: Calculate the angle
text: $$\frac{7\pi}{3}-\frac{6\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{3}.$$ Since the angles are coterminal, they land on the exact same point, meaning $$\sin\left(\frac{7\pi}{3}\right)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right).$$

title: Evaluate the special value
text: Recall your unit circle. The angle $$\frac{\pi}{3}$$ is in the first quadrant, where the $$y\$\$-coordinate$$ $$is$$ $$positive$$. $$The$$ $$y\$\$-coordinate$$ $$(sine)$$ $$at$$ $$this$$ $$angle$$ $$is$$ $$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$
